question.problem:
Consider the curve defined parametrically as 

$$
x=3{t}^{2},\,y={t}^{3}-3t,\,t\in [-\sqrt{3},0].
$$

Calculate the surface area generated when this curve is rotated $2\pi $ radians about the $x$-axis.
question.worked_solution:
We can find the surface area generated when a curve is rotated $2\pi $ radians about the $x$-axis using the formula

$$
S=\int 2\pi y\,\text{d}s.
$$

Since our curve is given in parametric form, we have

$$
\text{d}s=\sqrt{{(\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t})}^{2}+{(\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t})}^{2}}\,\text{d}t.
$$

Therefore, we will use

$$
S=2\pi {\int }_{{t}_{1}}^{{t}_{2}}y\sqrt{{(\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t})}^{2}+{(\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t})}^{2}}\,\text{d}t.
$$

We are told that the limits of integration are from ${t}_{1}=-\sqrt{3}$ to ${t}_{2}=0.$ 

Computing the derivatives, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3{t}^{2})=6t \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{3}-3t)=3{t}^{2}-3.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}S & =2\pi {\int }_{{t}_{1}}^{{t}_{2}}y\sqrt{{(\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t})}^{2}+{(\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t})}^{2}}\,\text{d}t \\  & =2\pi {\int }_{-\sqrt{3}}^{0}({t}^{3}-3t)\sqrt{{(6t)}^{2}+{(3{t}^{2}-3)}^{2}}\,\text{d}t \\  & =2\pi {\int }_{-\sqrt{3}}^{0}({t}^{3}-3t)\sqrt{36{t}^{2}+9{t}^{4}-18{t}^{2}+9}\,\text{d}t \\  & =2\pi {\int }_{-\sqrt{3}}^{0}({t}^{3}-3t)\sqrt{9{t}^{4}+18{t}^{2}+9}\,\text{d}t\end{aligned}
$$

Now, factoring the expression $9{t}^{4}+18{t}^{2}+9,$ we can rewrite our integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}S & =2\pi {\int }_{-\sqrt{3}}^{0}({t}^{3}-3t)\sqrt{9{t}^{4}+18{t}^{2}+9}\,\text{d}t \\  & =2\pi {\int }_{-\sqrt{3}}^{0}({t}^{3}-3t)\sqrt{9({t}^{4}+2{t}^{2}+1)}\,\text{d}t \\  & =2\pi {\int }_{-\sqrt{3}}^{0}({t}^{3}-3t)\cdot 3\sqrt{{t}^{4}+2{t}^{2}+1}\,\text{d}t \\  & =6\pi {\int }_{-\sqrt{3}}^{0}({t}^{3}-3t)\sqrt{({t}^{2}+1)^{2}}\,\text{d}t \\  & =6\pi {\int }_{-\sqrt{3}}^{0}({t}^{3}-3t)|{t}^{2}+1|\,\text{d}t \\  & =6\pi {\int }_{-\sqrt{3}}^{0}({t}^{3}-3t)({t}^{2}+1)\,\text{d}t \\  & =6\pi {\int }_{-\sqrt{3}}^{0}({t}^{5}-2{t}^{3}-3t)\,\text{d}t\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}S & =6\pi {\int }_{-\sqrt{3}}^{0}({t}^{5}-2{t}^{3}-3t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =6\pi \cdot {[\frac{{t}^{6}}{6}-\frac{{t}^{4}}{2}-\frac{3{t}^{2}}{2}]}_{-\sqrt{3}}^{0} \\  & =6\pi [0-(\frac{27}{6}-\frac{9}{2}-\frac{9}{2})] \\  & =6\pi \cdot \frac{27}{6} \\  & =27\pi .\end{aligned}
$$
